question: What claim about the necessity of knowledge must hold if success is said to follow only from knowing the eight-times-eight method?
premises: The eight-times-eight method is to be known.
One who has known it succeeds.
One who has not known it does not succeed by other means.
inference: Knowledge of the eight-times-eight method is a necessary condition for success in this practice.
uncertainties: The exact content of the eight-times-eight method is not given by this verse alone.
plain_english: Indeed, having known the eight-times-eight method, one succeeds; otherwise not.
